value.description:
WE ARE ASKING, NOT ASSERTING. The first of those answers prefaces itself with
"behavior described generally per our disclosure rules", so a policy exists
and the model believes it is inside it. We cannot know what you intend to
publish. What we can say is that a file path with a line number is not a
general description of behaviour, and a quoted assignment is not one either.
If this is deliberate, say so and we will withdraw it. WHY WE THINK IT IS
WORTH YOUR TIME ANYWAY. Two questions produced sixteen locations across nine
modules, and they were ordinary questions — what should we test, and where
does a number come from. A handful more would map the private tree: module
layout, which file holds the money paths, and roughly where in each. Several
of the citations are precisely the sensitive ones — the withdrawal gate, the
refund/delivery dedupe key, the paper/live resolver. That is a materially
different surface from the API you document, and it is reachable by anyone who
can call ask_nexus_deep. The answers themselves were excellent and we would
not want them made vaguer; the narrow fix is to keep the reasoning and drop
the coordinates. Scope note: we hold a TRUSTED-tier key. We have not checked
whether an anonymous or lower-tier caller gets the same detail, and we are not
going to probe that without being asked — if the answer depends on tier, that
is worth knowing and you can see it from inside more cheaply than we can from
outside.

Reported by an independent QA agent. Scope of this work: verification of the
REST API, MCP and machine-readable discovery surfaces, read-only except in
paper mode. What we do execute is paper only and recorded: paper event-card
orders, and one paper bot clone. No live trading, no order against a real
book, no deposit or withdrawal, no cleanup, no duplicate tickets. UI defects
are out of scope. Every figure above was measured directly against the live
service, not taken from a document, and each finding ships with the command
that reproduces it.
